title: Seller Pocket: Rapid Sprint Playsheet (v0)
summary: Pocket-sized, tactical playsheet for SEs/AE to run a fast technical sprint with platform or product engineering teams. Emphasis on diagnosing latency/cost constraints, proposing fallback routing and reserved capacity options, and capturing quick next steps.
audience: Field SEs, AEs engaging platform engineering, buyer technical champions (integration architects)
objectives: In 20–30 minutes: align on perf baseline, failure modes, and a short remediation plan
Enable seller to recommend 2 concrete immediate options (hosted fallback and dedicated pilot) with cost/latency tradeoffs
Capture a clear action list and handoff to Solutions/Onboarding
quick-setup: Pre-call: ask for a single sample endpoint, typical request size (tokens), and p95 latency target. If customer has synthetic load, ask for recent traces or load test report.
play_steps: 1) 5 min intro: confirm persona, success metric (latency p95, throughput qps, cost per 1M tokens)
2) 10 min triage: run rapid diagnostics (see checklist). Call out obvious mismatches (model mis-size, batch policy issues, sequence length spikes)
3) 5 min recommend: propose short list of mitigations and a pilot next-step (hosted canary, reserved capacity trial, private deployment assessment)
4) 5 min close: agree ownership, timeframe for pilot, and who will raise tickets (Solutions/SRE/Customer)
NOTE: keep recommendations prescriptive — include concrete config values when possible (batch_size=16, max_seq=512, quantization profile X-low-latency)
If time squeezed: skip deep kernel/infra talk; focus on routing and fallback economics
rapid-diagnostics: Ask for p50/p95/p99 token latency and tokens-per-request distribution
Confirm model identity + version + quantization used
Ask whether batching is enabled and typical batch sizes seen
Check for KV-cache usage patterns and any prefix reuse (few vs many unique prompts)
Look for sudden tail-latency spikes tied to seq length or cold-starts
canned-values-and-talk-tracks: One-liner value: 'Give us your slowest endpoint and we'll show a 2x reduction in p95 or a clear play to reserved capacity in 72 hours'
Host fallback pitch: 'Route burst traffic to a smaller/cheaper model for graceful degradation; keep high-quality model for low-latency/critical paths'
Dedicated pilot pitch: '4-week pilot with committed capacity, predictable p95, and cost modeling — includes SLO review and runbook'
Private pitch: 'If regulatory or data-control is the blocker, we can map a minimal VPC-onboard path with KMS integrations in parallel'
qualifying-questions: What is your p95 latency requirement and current p95?
What's your avg and 95th percentile tokens-per-request? (helps size batching & KV cache)
Are there data residency or audit constraints that would block hosted or dedicated?
Do you have traffic patterns (daily/hourly) or predictable scheduling windows?
standard-objections-and-scripts: Objection: 'We can't risk degraded quality by routing to a smaller model.' — Script: 'We only route non-critical flows or use a hybrid: small-model for short confirmations and large-model for long-form; we can A/B and measure quality with your eval set'
Objection: 'Dedicated is too expensive.' — Script: 'Let's run a 2-week burst analysis: estimate committed vs burst costs, and we can present an ROI with unit economics and break-even week'
Objection: 'We need on-prem for compliance.' — Script: 'We can scope a private pilot: minimal integration, clear timeline, and we keep the same API surface so dev work is minimal'
canary-and-hand-off-checklist: Define measurement: synthetic load profile + real traffic slice + observability hooks (tracing token-level)
Decide rollback criteria (error rate > X% or p95 degrade > Yms) and fallback target model/region
Create ticket with Solutions and SRE: include sample payloads, desired SLOs, and weekend/maintenance constraints
Schedule 30-minute post-canary review to capture learnings and next steps
pricing-and-econ-cheats: Rule of thumb: quantized model ~40–60% cheaper per-token; dedup/prefix cache can reduce billable tokens by 20–50% depending on reuse
Dedicated baseline: estimate committed GPU-hours -> translate to $/1M tokens using customer's avg tokens/request
Offer 'cost-limited fallback' to cap per-minute spend during spikes — good opener for risk-averse buyers
example-scripts: Opening (SE): 'Quick context check—what's the worst endpoint for you in production right now? We'll focus there and leave with a concrete pilot plan.'
Tie-down (AE): 'If we can hit p95 target in a 2-week pilot with an ROI sketch, is leadership likely to approve a reserved trial?'
Closing (SE/AE): 'I'll raise a ticket with Solutions and SRE. Who should be on the ticket from your side and what's the preferred 1-week window to run the canary?'
